subject: Private connectivity allowlist + outbound control next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Riley <ops-security@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity allowlist + outbound control next steps

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. To keep momentum on the private deployment for Acme Health, we need to lock the concrete allowlist and outbound control expectations. Attached is a simple CSV template (allowlist-template.csv) and a one-page sketch of the private VPC layout (private-vpc-sketch.pdf).

High-level ask: can your network team confirm the following by EOD Tue 2026-09-14?
- Primary static outbound IPs and any secondary ranges we should preserve for failover.
- Destination FQDNs (if you prefer FQDN allowlist for egress) and the ports you allow (typically 443).
- Whether outbound TLS inspection / outbound proxy will mutate SNI / require TLS pinning exceptions.
- Any maintenance windows or IP rotation cadence we should plan for.

If helpful, Marissa and Laura can run a short 30m config walkthrough with your infra team next week to align NAT/proxy expectations and confirm sample connections.

Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: allowlist-template.csv (stub), private-vpc-sketch.pdf (stub)

From: Tom Riley <ops-security@acmehealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Acme Health Network Team <network@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity allowlist + outbound control next steps

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the artifacts. A few clarifications from our side: we prefer to lock on IPs for egress to the Redwood control plane for auditability, but we run a proxy cluster in front of outbound which occasionally terminates TLS (TLS inspection). A couple of items: 
1) IP ranges: we can provide two /24s for your service to accept (primary+backup).
2) Ports: 443 only; we do not allow outbound 80 to external services.
3) TLS inspection: this means the client-side TLS fingerprint will differ; we need to know if Redwood supports certificate pinning exceptions or a proxy-friendly verification mode.
4) DNS: we may prefer FQDNs for human review, but acceptance will be on IP blocks in the firewall rules.

I can share the concrete CIDRs by EOD Monday 2026-09-13. If Redwood needs keepalives or health-check IPs on different ports, call that out.

Also looped in Naveen at our cloud vendor for questions about NAT stability.

—Tom
Director, Ops Security
Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Riley <ops-security@acmehealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity allowlist + outbound control next steps

Tom — looping in our networking and ops leads so we can turn your answers into a concrete mutual action plan. Summary of what we need from Acme to generate the final allowlist and firewall guidance: 
- Final egress CIDRs (two /24s if available) OR authoritative FQDN list you want to permit.
- Confirmation whether your outbound proxy will rewrite SNI or perform TLS MITM; if yes, provide TLS inspection cert details and whether OCSP stapling is preserved.
- Timezone windows for a 30-minute configuration test (we can do Tue/Wed 14:00-17:00 PT).
- Any legal/data residency constraints that affect routing (e.g., traffic must egress from a particular region).

Our deliverables after we receive answers: 
- A ready-to-import firewall CSV (allowlist-template.csv) with IPs/FQDNs and port columns.
- A short runbook for your firewall team describing connection verification and expected headers (SNI, X-Request-ID) for troubleshooting.
- An ops checklist for rotating IPs: how Redwood will notify and a 48-hour dual-accept window for any planned changes.

Next steps: if you can share the CIDRs by EOD Mon (2026-09-13) we will produce the draft CSV and runbook on Tue and schedule the 30m config test for Wed.

Thanks — Marissa
Enterprise Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachment: allowlist-template.csv (stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private connectivity allowlist + outbound control next steps

Tom — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment (Marissa, Laura, Hannah) we will: 
- Accept the two /24 CIDRs you provide and produce an import-ready CSV.
- Add explicit guidance for TLS inspection scenarios (pinning-exception field in the CSV and a short verification step for health checks).
- Provide a 48-hour dual-accept window where both old and new IPs are in the allowlist when rotations are scheduled.

Proposed plan and timeline:
1) You share CIDRs by EOD Mon 2026-09-13.
2) Redwood sends draft allowlist CSV + runbook Tue 2026-09-14 morning PT.
3) 30m config test Wed 2026-09-15 15:00 PT (we will send a calendar invite once you confirm).

If that works, please confirm and we'll lock the calendar.

Best —
Jonas
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: allowlist-template.csv (final draft will follow)
